info.title: Synthient API
info.description:
Synthient API for IP enrichment, account management, and real-time data feeds.

## Authentication

Every request needs an API key in the `X-Api-Key` header, `/health` included: the edge in front of `api.synthient.com` rejects a missing or malformed key with `401 text/plain` before the request reaches the API. Each operation lists the scopes that authorize it in `x-required-scopes` (any one suffices); a key without them gets `403` naming the scopes.

## Errors

Errors from the API are `application/problem+json` (`ProblemDetails`, or `ValidationProblemDetails` for 422). The edge's 401 is the one plain-text exception. Every response carries `X-Request-Id`, which is also the problem's `instance` — quote it when contacting support.

## Rate limits

Token buckets per team (organization), shared by all of its keys. Rate-limited responses carry `RateLimit-Limit` (the burst), `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`; a 429 from the limiter adds `Retry-After` (seconds).

| Operations | Sustained | Burst |
|---|---|---|
| `/lookup/ip/{ip_address}`, `/lookup/ips` (shared) | 100/s | 200 |
| `/lookup/domain/{domain}` | 20/min | 20 |
| `/account/me` | 10/s | 10 |
| Export list and meta, all feeds | 2/s | 60 |
| Export downloads, all feeds | 6/min | 120 |
| Stream connections, all feeds | 30/min | 20 |

A key's own monthly request budget, when set, also answers 429 once spent; an exhausted team credit balance answers 402.

## Feed Types

Each feed exposes two access patterns:
- **Stream** (`/stream`): Real-time NDJSON stream of live events. Connections stay open for up to 30 minutes; an empty NDJSON line is sent every ~15s as a transport-level keepalive that NDJSON parsers should skip.
- **Export** (`/export`): Pre-built parquet snapshots produced hourly and rolled up daily — list, download, and inspect metadata.

Each feed has its own dedicated section in the sidebar with full schema, scope, and cadence reference. Honeypot feeds are grouped under **Helios** (URL prefix `/feeds/helio/`, stream ids `honeypot_*`).

## Timestamps

Integer timestamps on the HTTP surface are Unix seconds (UTC), with two exceptions: the `timestamp` of anonymizer and Helios HTTP/HTTPS/DNS stream events is Unix **milliseconds** (as the sensors send it; their parquet exports use seconds), and `api_key.created_at` on `/account/me` is an RFC 3339 string. The same instants on the gRPC surface are encoded as `google.protobuf.Timestamp` (RFC 3339 strings under protojson, structured `{seconds, nanos}` under proto3 binary). Both representations refer to the same instant — only the encoding differs.

## API Versioning

The HTTP base path `/api/v4` is the *HTTP surface revision*. The gRPC service is `synthient.v1.SynthientService`. The two version numbers are decoupled by design — they were not bumped in lockstep historically and are not now. A breaking change to the gRPC contract bumps the proto package (v2, v3, …); a breaking change to the HTTP surface bumps the path revision (`/api/v5`).

## gRPC API

All HTTP endpoints have equivalent gRPC methods. The public gRPC endpoint is `grpc.synthient.com:443` (TLS). Do not use `api.synthient.com` or port `50051` — the internal gRPC port is not exposed publicly.

Example:

```
grpcurl -H 'x-api-key: YOUR_KEY' grpc.synthient.com:443 list
```

See the `synthient.v1.SynthientService` protobuf service definition for the full gRPC API. Authentication uses the `x-api-key` gRPC metadata key. Rate-limit rejections additionally carry a `retry-after` metadata field mirroring the HTTP `Retry-After` header.

get.summary: Stream Helios honeypot ADB shell commands in real time
get.description:
Real-time NDJSON stream of Android Debug Bridge shell commands captured by Helios honeypot sensors. Each event is one command in a session, ordered by `sequential_id`. Use the `session` field to reconstruct the full attacker shell transcript. Events carry no timestamp.

**Required scope:** `HONEYPOT_ADB_STREAM`. **Schema:** see `HoneypotADBStreamEntry` under Components.


get.summary: Stream Helios honeypot tunnel destinations in real time
get.description:
Real-time NDJSON stream of the destinations Helios honeypot tunnels were asked to reach: the host name (or address literal) and port, plus the proxy/server/pool metadata of the inbound tunnel. Despite the feed name, `domain` is the tunnel destination, not a DNS query name — the names resolved inside a tunneled DNS session are not visible.

**Required scope:** `HONEYPOT_DNS_STREAM`. **Schema:** see `HoneypotDNSStreamEntry` under Components.

**Sample event:**
```
{"timestamp":1714780800123,"tunnel_id":42,"domain":"api.ipify.org","port":443,"protocol":"dns","meta":{"proxy_ip":"203.0.113.10","server":"hp-eu-1","pool_id":"prod","provider":"luminati"}}
```
